title: Make verifier snapshot read-only; rerun once on fingerprint change
summary: The verifier will run against a snapshot it cannot write to (read-only permissions plus a write deny in its grant). If HEAD or the work tree still differs afterwards, the verdict is discarded and verification reruns once on a fresh snapshot, recording a system fault rather than a rejection of the work. Audience: Athena maintainers, who need verifier misbehaviour separated from bad work.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests for the write attempt and for the single rerun; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Prevent the write instead of only detecting it.
Change limited to the verifier run path and its tests.
Enforced by file permissions and a grant deny, not prose.
Behaviour exercised by tests run through cargo test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: No 'system fault' concept exists in the code (grep found none), so the producer adds a minimal one: a field on the verification/closing data and a ui line, not a new record schema.

Read-only is done by chmod on the verifier snapshot (as pin.rs make_read_only does) after checks, with a write-deny in the verifier grant if the grant type supports it; the .git dir stays writable only where git needs it, or is also locked.
Checks (run_check and restore_to) still need a writable snapshot, so lock only for the verifier agent's run and unlock afterwards.

If the rerun also differs, the job ends as a system fault and not as a rejection of the work; the old snapshot_changed blocker is removed or kept only for that second failure path, never as a work rejection.
Rerun happens at most once; the retry's cost counts against the verifier budget.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test shows that a write attempt in the verifier's snapshot (a file edit or a git commit) fails or is denied, and that the snapshot's HEAD and work-tree tree are unchanged afterwards. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test using the fake agent shows a changed snapshot fingerprint after the first verifier run triggers exactly one more verifier invocation on a freshly created snapshot, and that the first verdict is discarded.
A test shows that when the fingerprint changed, the outcome is recorded as a system fault, and the judgment does not contain the 'verifier changed its snapshot' rejection blocker or reject the work.
When the snapshot is unchanged, the verifier runs once and the verdict is used as before; existing tests still pass.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass on the workspace.
In run.rs the snapshot-changed branch near the old line 959 now discards the verdict and reruns once, and verify.rs no longer turns snapshot_changed into a blocker for the work.

out_of_scope: Changing the producer's snapshot or sandbox
Changing the check-tool configuration handling in toolconfig.rs
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
Changing how verdicts are judged apart from the snapshot-change path
departures: The change touches the verifier flow, permissions, a new fault concept and several tests, so cost and time sit above the reference and pass probability sits slightly below.
